messages:
sophia: FYI infra-bot just applied an ephemeral taint to gpu-node-73 after a short ECC/Xid burst. It didn't cordon+drain yet, just set gpu.health=degraded:NoSchedule. Thinking we should add a short pulse/recheck window before full drain to avoid preempting long-running Slurm jobs.

infra-bot: Signal: ECC_RATE=0.27 (threshold=0.2) detected on gpu-node-73; XID=4 within 45s. Action: TAINT gpu.health=degraded:NoSchedule (ephemeral). Logged incident id=inc-2064078901

alex: can you paste logs? want to check whether it's a driver-reset flood vs persistent ECC.

sophia: logs:
```
[ 21567.432108] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:04:00): 79, GPU reset triggered
[ 21567.432210] kernel: ecc: single-bit error corrected on device 0
[ 21568.512345] nv-host: reset completed
```

jonathan: sounds like transient resets. Proposal:
- pulse_wait = 90s
- require 2 independent samples over threshold OR reset_count >= 3 to escalate
- run a preflight NVML probe during pulse_wait; if it passes, clear taint
- only cordon+graceful-drain on failure/persistent errors

maya: also need Slurm behavior: if node has RUNNING jobs > 0 and any job has elapsed > 6h, prefer quarantine (move to quarantine partition) instead of immediate drain so we don't lose checkpt-unfriendly workloads.

sophia: suggested health rule config:
```
health_rules:
  ecc_spike:
    threshold: 0.2
    sample_window_s: 60
    pulse_wait_s: 90
    escalate_condition: "samples>=2 || resets>=3"
    preflight: "nvml_diag --quick"
    sanity_checks: [nvml_reachable, kubelet_heartbeat]
    actions: [taint, preflight_probe, cordon_and_drain_on_fail, schedule_replace_if_persistent]
```

alex: clarify preflight_probe semantics: synchronous probe that can clear the taint if OK within pulse_wait?

jonathan: exactly. infra-agent runs NVML quick diag + small tensor-run sanity check. If OK -> remove taint (kubectl taint ...-). If FAIL -> cordon then drain, honoring grace periods.

sophia: kubectl refs:
```
# ephemeral taint
kubectl taint nodes gpu-node-73 gpu.health=degraded:NoSchedule
# untaint on recovery
kubectl taint nodes gpu-node-73 gpu.health-
# cordon & drain if fail
kubectl cordon gpu-node-73
kubectl drain gpu-node-73 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --grace-period=300
```

maya: Slurm mapping:
```
scontrol update NodeName=gpu-node-73 State=DRAIN Reason="ecc-spike"
# resume on healthy
scontrol update NodeName=gpu-node-73 State=RESUME
```

ops-oncall: caution: network/telemetry blips can look like spikes when metrics are extrapolated. Add a telemetry sanity gate (nvml reachable, node heartbeat) before escalating to drain/replace.

sophia: will add heartbeat gate. Also recommend a small regional hot-spare pool (eu-west1-hotspare) to absorb drains so regional capacity SLOs don't break.

jonathan: and rate limits: max_concurrent_drains_per_rack=1 and global_rate_limit=1 node / 12m. Prevent cascade if rack experiences power glitch.

alex: i'll stub a PR for the rule changes and test on canary pool tonight. can someone add a unit test simulating 2-sample bounce + intermittent network loss?

ops-oncall: i'll run a chaos sim: inject Xid bursts + telemetry blips on canary. Will validate we don't mass-drain. :thumbsup:

infra-bot: Scheduled chaos job: chaos-ecc-burst-2064079999 queued for canary at 2026-03-19T02:00:00Z

maya: if canary passes, roll to prod with 72h close monitoring & automatic rollback if replacements > 2 per rack in 24h.

sophia: thanks team. Opening PR now and will post the link and CI results here.
